topics.topic_label: Inference cost economics (Sandisk and SK hynix publish the first OCP specification for High Bandwidth Flash — a vendor-neutral tier between HBM and SSD, 512GB modules at 0.4–3.0 TB/s, with Google and Tenstorrent joining during standardisation — which is the concrete follow-through on the argument that storage becomes the inference bottleneck once KV caches outgrow system memory; on the demand side Pinecone makes budget a first-class query primitive)

Semiconductor & compute supply chain (the first OCP specification for High Bandwidth Flash defines the xPU-HBF host interface, electrical guidelines and packaging for a die stack six months after the workstream formed — getting two memory vendors plus Google to agree on the host interface this early is the part that usually doesn't happen; Samsung previews zHBM, zNAND-O and the first V10 BV-NAND at the same summit)

Inference cost economics (AMD buys Taalas to etch model weights directly into silicon - an explicit moat play against commoditization by Chinese open-weight models, with the obvious counter running through the replies that etched weights cannot be updated so the economics only work if model churn slows; meanwhile the effort dial ships as a product control, DeepSeek warns of a price rise, and a small open model does retrieval at 1/100th the cost)
